quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When passing a parked car on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, assume the driver may open the door suddenly. Drive carefully near parked vehicles.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Slow down when driving in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread depth and proper air pressure. Also slow down in the rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
To get other drivers moving in a traffic jam.
When you are angry with another driver.
To say hello to another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when it helps prevent a crash. It gets the attention of drivers who may not see you.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
Trucks are on the upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: Why is a space cushion around your vehicle important?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic flowing at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special seats made for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper child seat for children too small for regular seatbelts.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left at this location.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. This means:

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Massachusetts law requires headlights to be used:

options.text: From one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise.
When the temperature drops below freezing.
During the day in good weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: From one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Headlights help you see better when it is dark.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You can only park on a freeway shoulder if you have an emergency.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell you to yield. You can go when the road is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: What helps drivers avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Adding extra weight to the vehicle for better grip.
Leaving the highway as fast as possible.
Slowing down and keeping more distance from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down and keeping more distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice and stay farther behind other vehicles. These are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest thing to do is:

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or road narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines divide lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines divide lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic speed.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, you should:

options.text: Drive normally because emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because you are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Call a friend while driving to talk about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions distract you from driving. If you are worried, excited, angry, sad, or crying, take time to calm down before you drive.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a tiny amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills suffer immediately. Never drink and drive.
